title: STL Clear Memory Leak (Non-Shrinking Capacity)
pattern: Calling `clear()` on a standard library vector/collection to release memory.
why_bad: `std::vector::clear()` resets the size but keeps the allocated heap capacity, leaving unused memory bound to the object and starving the system allocator.
detection: Invocation of `clear()` on a large vector whose lifetime extends far past the clearance point, without subsequent reallocation.
counterexample: The vector will be refilled immediately with a similar volume of data. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Swap the vector with a default-constructed empty temporary: `std::vector<float>().swap(data)`.
source: *The Art of Readable Code*, Chapter 5, "Advertising Likely Pitfalls" (p. 52 / 573).
